extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy, law, and governance (general educated audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards and normative principles for constituting and evaluating political bodies, public ministers, property distribution, trade organization, and public finance as set out in a classic political-theory treatise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly acts bind only assenting members
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatsoever unlawfull Act is decreed, is the Act onely of those that assented, and not of any that dissented, or were absent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An assembly's decree does not bind those who dissent or are absent; liability for an unlawful act lies with those who voted for it or assisted in executing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial limits on assembly jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: An Assembly residing out of the bounds of that Colony whereof they have the government, cannot execute any power over the persons, or goods of any of the Colonie ... as having no Jurisdiction, nor Authoritie elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An assembly or corporate body's authority does not extend beyond the territorial bounds of the polity that created it; remedies outside that territory are left to local law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemblies' inability to execute penalties outside their territory
rubrics_metrics.description: Though the Assembly have right, to impose a Mulct upon any of their members, that shall break the Lawes they make; yet out of the Colonie it selfe, they have no right to execute the same
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A body may legislate or fine members but cannot carry out punitive executions beyond its own jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereign cognisance of complaints against bodies politick
rubrics_metrics.description: If any particular member conceive himself Injured by the Body it self, the Cognisance of his cause belongeth to the Soveraign, and those the Soveraign hath ordained for Judges in such causes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disputes between individuals and corporate bodies are properly adjudicated by the sovereign or its appointed judges, not by the offending body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative form for foreign trade bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: For the well ordering of forraigne Trafficke, the most commodious Representative is an Assembly of all the members; that is to say, such a one, as every one that adventureth his mony, may be present at all the Deliberations, and Resolutions of the Body, if they will themselves
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merchant corporations used for foreign trade should be governed by assemblies in which every investor can attend deliberations, because the corporate end is the private gain of adventurers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporations for trade create double monopoly
rubrics_metrics.description: To grant to a Company of Merchants to be a Corporation, or Body Politique, is to grant them a double Monopoly, whereof one is to be sole buyers; another to be sole sellers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corporate monopolies concentrate buying and selling power (sole buyer at home, sole seller abroad), benefiting adventurers but harming the domestic populace and foreigners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monopoly harms domestic and foreign interests
rubrics_metrics.description: One part is disadvantageous to the people at home, the other to forraigners ... by their sole exportation they set what price they please on the husbandry and handy-works of the people; and by the sole importation, what price they please on all forraign commodities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monopolistic corporations can raise or lower prices to the detriment of certain groups; ideally corporations should be confined to foreign markets while domestic trade remains free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and member participation in merchant bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: The end then of these Bodies of Merchants ... it is reason that every one be acquainted with the employment of his own; that is, that every one be of the Assembly, that shall have the power to order the same; and be acquainted with their accounts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the corporate end is the private gain of adventurers, representatives should allow members to participate and inspect accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for corporate debts to strangers
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Body Politique of Merchants, contract a debt to a stranger by the act of their Representative Assembly, every Member is lyable by himself for the whole
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creditors unfamiliar with internal corporate law treat members as jointly liable until payment by one discharges the rest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creditor remedy for debts owed to company by member
rubrics_metrics.description: If one of the Members be indebted to the Body, he may be sued by the Body; but his goods cannot be taken, nor his person imprisoned by the authority of the Body; but only by Authority of the Common-wealth
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A corporate body may sue a member, but cannot itself execute coercive penalties (seizure/imprisonment); enforcement requires sovereign authority to avoid bodies judging their own cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment of public taxes on corporate members
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Common-wealth impose a Tax upon the Body, it is understood to be layd upon every member proportionably to his particular adventure in the Company
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the state taxes a corporate body, the burden falls on members proportionally to their shares/adventures; there is typically no separate common stock beyond members' contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for unlawful corporate acts limited to active participants
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Mulct be layd upon the Body for some unlawfull act, they only are lyable by whose votes the act was decreed, or by whose assistance it was executed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only those who voted for or aided the unlawful act are liable; mere membership alone is not criminality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited representative bodies convened to advise sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: Such Deputies, having a place and time of meeting assigned them, are there, and at that time, a Body Politique ... but it is onely for such matters as shall be propounded unto them by that Man, or Assembly, that by the Soveraign Authority sent for them; and when it shall be declared that nothing more shall be propounded, nor debated by them ... the Body is dissolved
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegated advisory bodies represent the people only for the specific matters assigned by the sovereign and cease once their remit is exhausted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegates' scope limited by writ of summons
rubrics_metrics.description: For the limits of how farre such a Body shall represent the whole People, they are set forth in the Writing by which they were sent for. For the People cannot choose their Deputies to other intent, than is in the Writing directed to them from their Soveraign expressed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deputies cannot be legitimately authorized for purposes beyond those specified in the sovereign's writ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private regular bodies (families) lawful within law
rubrics_metrics.description: Private Bodies Regular, and Lawfull, are those that are constituted without Letters ... such as are all Families, in which the Father, or Master ordereth the whole Family ... he obligeth his Children, and Servants, as farre as the Law permitteth
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic households are regular lawful bodies with a representative (head) whose authority extends only so far as civil law permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private regular but unlawful bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Private Bodies Regular, but Unlawfull, are those that unite themselves into one person Representative, without any publique Authority at all; such as are the Corporations of Beggars, Theeves and Gipsies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups that self-incorporate without public authority, especially for unlawful ends, are illicit corporate forms and threaten the commonwealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leagues and irregular systems judged by their purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Irregular Systemes ... become Lawfull, or Unlawfull, according to the lawfulnesse, or unlawfulnesse of every particular mans design therein
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private leagues are lawful or unlawful depending on members' aims; among subjects of one commonwealth such leagues often savour of faction and are suspect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leagues among subjects often unnecessary and dangerous
rubrics_metrics.description: The Leagues of Subjects ... are in a Common-wealth for the most part unnecessary, and savour of unlawfull designe; and are for that cause Unlawfull, and go commonly by the name of factions, or Conspiracies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because sovereign power can provide rights and defence, private alliances among subjects can be redundant, dangerous, and may be treated as conspiracies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret cabals within assemblies are unlawful factions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Soveraign Power be in a great Assembly, and a number of men, part of the Assembly, without authority, consult a part, to contrive the guidance of the rest; This is a Faction, or Conspiracy unlawfull
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subgroups secretly maneuvering inside a sovereign assembly to manipulate outcomes constitute unlawful seduction of the assembly for private interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal lobbying to gather supporters (not necessarily unjust)
rubrics_metrics.description: But if he, whose private interest is to be debated, and judged in the Assembly, make as many friends as he can; in him it is no Injustice ... And though he hire such friends with mony ... yet it is not Injustice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person soliciting support for his own cause is not necessarily guilty of faction; paid support is not per se unjust unless expressly outlawed—Hobbes notes the pragmatic reality that justice may require money.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private armies/feuds unlawful within a commonwealth
rubrics_metrics.description: If a private man entertain more servants, than the government of his estate, and lawfull employment he has for them requires, it is Faction, and unlawfull
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining private force beyond what lawful employment requires undermines public security and is treated as faction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factions based on religion or class are unjust
rubrics_metrics.description: Factions for Kindred ... Factions for Government of Religion ... or of State ... are unjust, as being contrary to the peace and safety of the people
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organized groups formed around kin, religion, or political class that challenge sovereign authority jeopardize peace and are condemned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concourse of people lawful only when occasion and number appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Concourse of people, is an Irregular Systeme, the lawfulnesse, or unlawfullnesse, whereof dependeth on the occasion, and on the number of them that are assembled ... If the occasion be lawfull, and manifest, the Concourse is lawfull ... if the numbers be extraordinarily great, the occasion is not evident
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemblies are lawful when purpose is manifest and size ordinary; extraordinarily large gatherings without clear purpose may be judged tumultuous and unlawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unlawful tumult when assembly number disproportionate to purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be lawfull for a thousand men, to joyn in a Petition ... yet if a thousand men come to present it, it is a tumultuous Assembly; because there needs but one or two for that purpose
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appropriateness of numbers is judged by necessity of the purpose—unnecessary large numbers assembling against an accused create unlawful tumult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Publique Minister
rubrics_metrics.description: A PUBLIQUE MINISTER, is he, that by the Soveraign ... is employed in any affaires, with Authority to represent in that employment, the Person of the Common-wealth
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only those serving the sovereign in public/political capacities (not merely servants in a natural capacity) are public ministers; household officers without public administrative authority are not public ministers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers for general administration act in sovereign name
rubrics_metrics.description: Of Publique Ministers, some have charge committed to them of a general Administration ... every Subject is so far obliged to obedience, as the Ordinances he shall make, and the commands he shall give be in the Kings name, and not inconsistent with his Soveraign Power
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governors/regents/vice-roys bind subjects only insofar as their ordinances are issued in the sovereign's name and do not infringe sovereign rights; commissions do not transfer sovereignty without express words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers of public finance
rubrics_metrics.description: They that have Authority concerning the Treasure, as Tributes, Impositions, Rents, Fines, or whatsoever publique revenue, to collect, receive, issue, or take the Accounts thereof, are Publique Ministers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collectors, receivers, treasurers are public ministers responsible for gathering and disbursing public revenue; they act by sovereign authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers of militia and war are public ministers
rubrics_metrics.description: They that have Authority concerning the Militia; to have the custody of Armes, Forts, Ports; to Levy, Pay, or Conduct Souldiers; or to provide for any necessary thing for the use of war, either by Land or Sea, are publique Ministers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders and officers with authority over armed forces represent the sovereign and are public ministers; a soldier without command does not represent the commonwealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers of instruction and judicature
rubrics_metrics.description: They also that have authority to teach ... are Publique Ministers ... They also to whom Jurisdiction is given, are Publique Ministers. For in their Seats of Justice they represent the person of the Soveraign; and their Sentence, is his Sentence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers and judges who act by sovereign mandate are public ministers; judges render the sovereign's sentence and must observe impartial procedures to avoid judging in their own cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duality of judicial functions (fact vs law) and impartial judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Controversies are of two sorts, namely of Fact, and of Law; so are judgements, some of Fact, some of Law ... there may be two Judges, one of Fact, another of Law ... no man can be Judge in his own cause
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal processes should separate fact-finding and legal judgement where appropriate; parties may except biased judges and appeal to others or the sovereign as final arbiter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on status of envoys and private missions
rubrics_metrics.description: Publique Ministers abroad, are those that represent the Person of their own Soveraign, to forraign States ... such as are sent by Authoritie only of some private partie ... are neither Publique, nor Private Ministers of the Common-wealth
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only agents sent by public authority on public business represent the commonwealth abroad; envoys sent by private parties or for a natural capacity do not carry sovereign imprimatur, even if received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counsellors without judicial/administrative power are not public ministers
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither a Counsellor, nor a Councell of State, if we consider it with no Authority of Judicature or Command, but only of giving Advice ... is a Publique Person
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory bodies lacking actual administrative or judicial authority do not themselves represent the sovereign, unless vested with further powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nutrition of commonwealth defined (commodities, preparation, distribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NUTRITION of a Common-wealth consisteth, in the Plenty, and Distribution of Materials conducing to Life: In Concoction, or Preparation; and (when concocted) in the Conveyance of it, by convenient conduits, to the Publique use
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A state's 'nourishment' comprises native and foreign commodities, their preparation (money as a medium), and distribution; plenty depends primarily on labour and industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereign control of property distribution and contract rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Distribution of the Materials of this Nourishment ... belongeth in all kinds of Common-wealth to the Soveraign Power ... it belongeth to the Common-wealth ... to appoint in what manner, all kinds of contract between Subjects ... are to bee made
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules of property, land division, contracts (sale, loan, hire, etc.) and the allocation of trade locations/commodities are sovereign prerogatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private property subordinated to sovereign domain
rubrics_metrics.description: The Propriety which a subject hath in his lands, consisteth in a right to exclude all other subjects from the use of them; and not to exclude their Soveraign
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject's property excludes other subjects but remains ultimately under sovereign dominion; sovereign can alter distributions for common peace/security though abuses are breach of trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocating fixed public revenues is vain and unsafe
rubrics_metrics.description: The setting forth of Publique Land, or of any certaine Revenue for the Common-wealth, is in vaine; and tendeth to the dissolution of Government ... The Publique Riches cannot be limited by other limits, than those which the emergent occasions shall require
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigning fixed estates or revenues to public maintenance is ineffective because representatives may alienate or mismanage them; public finance must respond to emergent needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Money as the 'blood' of the commonwealth
rubrics_metrics.description: By Concoction ... this is nothing else but Gold, and Silver, and Mony ... this Concoction, is as it were the Sanguification of the Common-wealth
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portable, widely valued money (gold/silver) functions as the medium that circulates value across the polity; base or local coinage is more fragile and subject to debasement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public financial conduits and officers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Conduits, and Wayes by which it is conveyed to the Publique use, are of two sorts; One, that Conveyeth it to the Publique Coffers; The other, that Issueth the same out againe ... Of the first sort, are Collectors, Receivers, and Treasurers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public finance requires collectors/receivers/treasurers to collect revenue and officers to issue payments; these are parts of the state's organic structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colonies as procreation of commonwealth
rubrics_metrics.description: The Procreation, or Children of a Common-wealth, are those we call Plantations, or Colonies; which are numbers of men sent out from the Common-wealth, under a Conductor, or Governour, to inhabit a Forraign Country
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colonies are extensions of a commonwealth, established under leadership to inhabit and exploit foreign territories; they are part of the polity's procreative/expansive functions.
